newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp workers down tools over job fears.
newsitem.headline: Krupp workers down tools over job fears.

text.p: Around 1,000 workers fearful of losing their jobs at German steelmaker Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG downed tools briefly on Tuesday to hold a protest meeting, the company's works council said.

They were demonstrating against a management cost-cutting plan which foresees reducing the Krupp workforce by 2,000 workers. The "optimisation plan" will be reviewed by the company's supervisory board on February 5.

The demonstrators were joined by workers from the Bochum and Siegerland works in the Germany's industrial Ruhr region. Steel production at Krupp's Dortmund Westfalenhuette works was reduced during the protest.
The strategy also proposes carrying out a 450 million mark ($272 million) refit of Krupp's Dortmund Hoerde works, while union leaders are calling for the building of a completely new plant.

Worker discontent has been fuelled by newspaper reports that Krupp and Thyssen would merge some of their steel operations. Thyssen chief executive Dieter Vogel and Krupp CEO Hans-Wilhelm Grasshof have rejected the reports.
Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG is part of the steel division of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp., and produces long steel products.
